paper.title_en: Quantifying quantum coherence via the interpolated Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability
paper.abstract_en: As a fundamental feature of quantum mechanics, coherence plays an essential role in quantum information processing. In recent years, an increasing number of studies have focused on characterizing quantum coherence using the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD) quasiprobability distribution. In this paper, we introduce a new coherence quantifier based on the interpolated KD quasiprobability and systematically examine its key properties. An upper bound for this measure is derived, and its relationship with the $l_{1}$-norm coherence is discussed. Moreover, we propose an analogous coherence measure defined via the imaginary part of the interpolated KD distribution and compare it with existing coherence quantifiers Finally, several concrete examples are provided to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach.
